applies_why: The judge text decides a Matthew 1:16 link by isolating that verse's Greek as ambiguous, which is the verse-level collision K-C governs.
quote: the passive egennēthē (was born) with feminine hēs (of whom) admits both the withheld-father and the birth-narration readings
rule_words: the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires
room: never verse by verse: (1) bars treating Matthew 1:16's own ambiguity as decisive without chain-by-footing; (2) permits noting a verse admits both readings as one step within chain weighing.
why: The judge's stated reason is Matthew 1:16's own verbal ambiguity, so it resolves the link verse by verse rather than weighing the pressed chains by footing as K-C requires.
